10.3.1: General Characteristics of Alkaline Earth Metals
All alkaline earth metals are silvery white metals possessing metallic luster. However they lose the metallic luster when exposed to the atmosphere.
Alkaline earth metals are silvery white (grayish) elements harder than alkali metals. They are malleable and ductile possessing metallic luster.

In alkali metals there is a single valence electron due to which metallic bond is too weak but in alkaline earth metals there are two valence electrons making stronger metallic bond. Alkali metals are soft because of weak metallic bond and alkaline earth metals are harder due to strong metallic bond.
Alkaline earth metals have large atomic size but smaller than corresponding alkali metals. Atomic size increases down the group.
Both atomic and ionic radii increase on moving down the group because new electron is added to new shell at each step which increases the shielding effect and nuclear distance.

Low density of alkaline earth metals is due to their relatively larger atomic size as a result atoms are less densely packed.
